title: One day of New York's water
description: New York uses about a billion gallons of water a day, enough to flood Central Park more than 3½ feet deep. This 3D map of Midtown pours one day of it into the skyline's landmarks in turn: the Empire State Building is full by 5:42 am, then the Chrysler Building, One Vanderbilt and 30 Rock, with the Bank of America Tower 44% full at midnight. Switch to 1991, when the city used 47% more, and the water gets through the MetLife Building into 432 Park Avenue. Tower volumes come from each building's 3D shape in OpenStreetMap; water use from NYC Open Data.
